haiku-low.q2: Up to 90 minutes after its updated_at, because a bulk import can make a row visible late. Lookback is 2 hours.
haiku-low.q3: A later nightly run re-reads rows with updated_at after its cutoff; the merge upserts by order_id, and the newer updated_at wins.
haiku-low.q4: The merge sets is_deleted to true when deleted_at is set.
haiku-low.q5: Logs it as failed. Under three failures for the night, waits 15 minutes and retries from extract; at three, pages on-call.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards read fact_orders at 06:00 whatever its state, showing the whole previous night. #data-alerts gets a staleness alert from the 06:00 check.
haiku-low.q7: Sunday reconciliation finds the mismatched day by comparing counts and checksums with the replica, then reloads that day from the replica.
haiku-low.q8: The merge replaces an existing order only when the staged updated_at is equal or newer, so an older or duplicate copy never overwrites.
haiku-low.q9: In etl_watermark, one row, set to the time the read started. It is written in the same transaction as the merge, so only on commit.
haiku-low.q10: The merge is one transaction, so dashboards see either the whole previous night or the whole new one, never half-loaded.
haiku-low.q11: Extract empties stg_orders and rewrites it. The watermark is unchanged, so the retry uses the same cutoff, watermark minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads all that day's replica rows, ignoring the watermark, and merges them as in step 3. The watermark does not move.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler at 02:00 UTC starts it. It extracts every replica `orders` row with `updated_at` after the cutoff, which is the watermark minus 2 hours.
sonnet.q2: The document says a bulk import can make a row visible up to 90 minutes after its `updated_at`. It does not say why this happens.
sonnet.q3: A later nightly run re-reads the edited row because its `updated_at` is after the cutoff. The merge upserts it by `order_id`, and it replaces the existing row when the staged `updated_at` is equal or newer.
sonnet.q4: The merge sets `is_deleted` to true in `fact_orders` when `deleted_at` is set. The row is not removed. The document does not say how the app deletes the order, such as whether it sets `deleted_at` and `updated_at`.
sonnet.q5: The failure is logged as failed in `etl_runs`. A merge failure rolls back, so `fact_orders` and the watermark are unchanged. Step 4 then counts the night's failed attempts. With fewer than 3 it waits 15 minutes and starts a new attempt at extract. At 3 failures it pages on-call.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards read `fact_orders` as it stands, which is the whole previous night's data. If `etl_runs` has no committed merge since 02:00, the 06:00 check posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts. Page on-call happens only after 3 failed attempts.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares per-day row counts and checksums of `order_id` plus `updated_at` for the last 30 days between the replica and `fact_orders`. For a day that differs, it re-reads all of that day's rows from the replica, ignoring the watermark, and merges them.
sonnet.q8: The merge upserts by `order_id`. An existing row is replaced only when the staged `updated_at` is equal or newer, so an older copy never overwrites a newer one. A duplicate with an equal `updated_at` just replaces the row with the same version.
sonnet.q9: It is the one row in `etl_watermark` in the warehouse. The value is the time step 2 started reading, not when the read ended. It is set inside the merge transaction and committed together with the `fact_orders` changes.
sonnet.q10: The merge is one warehouse transaction that writes `fact_orders` and the watermark together. Dashboards therefore see either the whole previous night or the whole new one.
sonnet.q11: The document does not say what happens to rows staged by a failed attempt, apart from the following. Extract empties `stg_orders` and rewrites it on each attempt, so earlier staged rows are replaced. A failed merge rolls back, so `fact_orders` and the watermark are unchanged. The retry reads the watermark again and extracts rows with `updated_at` after watermark minus 2 hours, which is the same window as before because the watermark did not move.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads all of the mismatched day's rows from the replica, ignoring the watermark. It merges them as in step 3, an upsert by `order_id` where the newer or equal `updated_at` wins. It does not change the watermark.
